story:
Tusker is a boar of the south-western beeches of Cornwall as big as a hay-cart, and the ground under the beeches where he roots is turned as if a plough had been through it. The hunters of Cornwall Station named him for his tusks, which are as long as a man's forearm and yellow with age, and they have never agreed on anything else about him: how old he is, what he eats besides beech-mast, or whether the giant rooters of the woods are his children.

The Cornish say the great boars are the oldest beasts of the west. In their songs a boar runs ahead of the king's hunt across the whole of the land and cannot be caught, and leaves the valleys behind him where his tusks went through the hills. The drovers do not say Tusker is that boar. They do not say he is not.

He has never charged a herd or a man who left him to his rooting, and the Hexts drive their cattle within a spear's throw of him every season. The hunters who did not leave him alone have a saying: Tusker turns the ground for the beeches, and for anyone who interrupts him.
legend: Tusker is a giant boar in the south-western beeches of Cornwall, level 45. He never aggros, so you can walk past him. If you want him, he is a plain melee mob with no spells, a solid fight at 45: bring a group in the mid forties with a tank who can hold him. The giant rooters around him are easy but do aggro, so clear them. He comes back fast (the data says 80 seconds).

aggro: Tusker looks up from the mast. He is not pleased.
The great boar lowers his tusks.
